item.title: AI Is Eating Software, but Embodiment May Eat the World
item.description: As software generation gets cheaper, one of the next major sources of scarcity may be the interface between intelligence and reality.

item.title: AI Is Eating Software, but Embodiment May Eat the World
item.description: As software generation gets cheaper, the next scarce frontier may be the interface between intelligence and reality.

item.title: How Does a Smart Outsider Enter a Hard Domain?
item.description: Hard domains are rarely entered through instant legitimacy. More often, smart outsiders earn their way in through contact, judgment, and a narrow wedge of real usefulness.

item.title: Robotics Commercialization
item.description: In robotics, the hard part is rarely making the machine work once. It is making the system deployable, trustworthy, and economically useful at scale.

item.title: Where Should an Innovative Engineer Move Next in the Age of AI
item.description: As software implementation gets cheaper, the strongest engineering leverage may move toward domains where intelligence must survive contact with reality.

item.title: Where Should an Innovative Engineer Move Next in the Age of AI
item.description: The strongest engineering leverage in the AI era may shift away from pure implementation and toward robotics, infrastructure, industrial systems, and other domains where intelligence meets messy reality.
